# Example Org Risk Assessment and Authorization Standard

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This Standard establishes Example Org's requirements for risk assessment, security categorization, control assessment, authorization, continuous monitoring, penetration testing, risk response, and related contingency planning activities. It applies to all Example Org information systems, system components, and services that process, store, or transmit organizational information, including electronic protected health information where applicable.

## 2. Roles and Responsibilities

Security Program / GRC owns the risk assessment and authorization process end-to-end. Security Program / GRC performs or coordinates risk assessments, security categorizations, control assessments, continuous monitoring, penetration testing coordination, risk response, and authorization support activities described in this Standard; maintains the risk register and the authorization decision record; and is accountable for ensuring the process operates at the cadence specified below. Other functions — including system owners, authorizing officials, independent assessors, penetration testing agents, and workforce members generally — participate in individual steps as identified in each section, but Security Program / GRC is accountable for the process and for the handoffs between participants.

Unless a requirement below identifies a different responsible party, Security Program / GRC performs, reviews, or answers for the described activity.

## 3. Policy and Procedures

- Security Program / GRC must develop, document, and disseminate an organization-level (and/or mission/business-process-level or system-level) risk assessment policy to [Designated Personnel or Roles] that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; Security Program / GRC must also develop procedures to facilitate implementation of the policy and associated risk assessment controls. [NIST 800-53 RA-1 | ARC-AMPE RA-1 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must develop, document, and disseminate an organization-level (and/or mission/business-process-level or system-level) assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy to [Designated Personnel or Roles] that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; Security Program / GRC must also develop procedures to facilitate implementation of the policy and associated assessment, authorization, and monitoring controls. [NIST 800-53 CA-1 | ARC-AMPE CA-1 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must designate an official to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the risk assessment policy and procedures, and a designated official to do the same for the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and procedures. [NIST 800-53 RA-1 | ARC-AMPE RA-1 AE Mandatory | NIST 800-53 CA-1 | ARC-AMPE CA-1 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must review and update the risk assessment policy and procedures, and the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and procedures, annually and following [Defined Events] (such as assessment or audit findings, security or privacy incidents/breaches, or changes in applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, or guidelines), consistent with ARC-AMPE's requirement that this review occur at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events. [NIST 800-53 RA-1 | ARC-AMPE RA-1 AE Mandatory | NIST 800-53 CA-1 | ARC-AMPE CA-1 AE Mandatory]
- Example Org must implement reasonable and appropriate policies and procedures to comply with the applicable security rule requirements, taking into account specified factors; such policies and procedures may be changed at any time provided changes are documented and implemented in accordance with the rule. [HIPAA 164.316(a)]
- Security Program / GRC must maintain implemented policies and procedures, and any required documentation of actions, activities, or assessments, in written (which may be electronic) form; retain such documentation for 6 years from the date of creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later; make the documentation available to persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which it pertains; and review the documentation periodically, updating it as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information. [HIPAA 164.316(b)(1) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(i) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(ii) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(iii)]
- Example Org must identify the security official responsible for the development and implementation of the required security policies and procedures. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(2)]
- Security Program / GRC must implement policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(1)(i)]

## 4. Security Categorization

- Security Program / GRC must categorize the system and the information it processes, stores, and transmits; document the security categorization results, including supporting rationale, in the system security plan and in the risk register; and verify that the authorizing official (or designated representative) reviews and approves the security categorization decision. [NIST 800-53 RA-2 | ARC-AMPE RA-2 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must conduct impact-level prioritization of organizational systems to obtain additional granularity on system impact levels. [NIST 800-53 RA-2(1)]

## 5. Risk Assessment

- Security Program / GRC must conduct a risk assessment that identifies threats to and vulnerabilities in the system, determines the likelihood and magnitude of harm from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction of the system and its information, and determines the likelihood and impact of adverse effects on individuals arising from processing of personally identifiable information; risk assessment results and risk management decisions from organization and mission/business process perspectives must be integrated with system-level risk assessments. [NIST 800-53 RA-3 | ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must document risk assessment results in the risk register together with security and privacy plans, a risk assessment report, or another organization-defined document; per ARC-AMPE, documentation must appear in the Information System Risk Assessment (ISRA), Security Assessment Report (SAR), and privacy plans (e.g., PIA). [NIST 800-53 RA-3 | ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must review risk assessment results annually or when a significant change occurs, consistent with ARC-AMPE's requirement to review at least every one (1) year or when a significant change occurs, and must disseminate risk assessment results to [Designated Personnel or Roles]. [NIST 800-53 RA-3 | ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must update the risk assessment annually, or when there are significant changes to the system, its environment of operation, or other conditions that may impact its security or privacy state; this satisfies ARC-AMPE's minimum requirement to update at least every three (3) years, before issuing a new internal/organization-specific authorization, or upon significant change. [NIST 800-53 RA-3 | ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must document and implement a privacy risk management process that assesses privacy risk to individuals resulting from the collection, sharing, storing, transmitting, use, and disposal of PII. [ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must assess supply chain risks associated with [Designated Systems, System Components, and System Services], and must update the supply chain risk assessment annually, when there are significant changes to the relevant supply chain, or when changes to the system, environments of operation, or other conditions may necessitate a change. [NIST 800-53 RA-3(1)]
- Security Program / GRC must use all-source intelligence, including publicly available/open-source information, to assist in the analysis of risk, to inform engineering, acquisition, and risk management decisions, and to analyze risk of vulnerabilities from development, manufacturing, and delivery processes, people, and the environment. [NIST 800-53 RA-3(2) | ARC-AMPE RA-3(2) AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must determine the current cyber threat environment on an ongoing basis using [Designated Means]. [NIST 800-53 RA-3(3)]
- Security Program / GRC must employ [Advanced Automation and Analytics Capabilities] to predict and identify risks to [Designated Systems or System Components]. [NIST 800-53 RA-3(4)]
- Security Program / GRC must conduct an accurate and thorough assessment of potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronic protected health information held by Example Org. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A)]
- Security Program / GRC must implement security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(B)]
- Security Program / GRC must ensure appropriate sanctions are applied against workforce members who fail to comply with security policies and procedures. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(C)]
- Security Program / GRC must implement procedures to regularly review records of information system activity, such as audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D)]
- Security Program / GRC must perform a periodic technical and nontechnical evaluation, initially based on the standards implemented under the security rule and subsequently in response to environmental or operational changes affecting ePHI security, establishing the extent to which security policies and procedures meet the rule's requirements. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(8)]

## 6. Criticality Analysis

- Security Program / GRC must identify critical system components and functions by performing a criticality analysis for [Designated Systems, System Components, or System Services] at [Designated Decision Points] in the system development life cycle; per ARC-AMPE, all system components within the CMS ATC/RTC boundary (or equivalent State AE/other ARC-AMPE user boundary) are considered critical. [NIST 800-53 RA-9 | ARC-AMPE RA-9 AE Mandatory]

## 7. Control Assessments

- Security Program / GRC must select the appropriate assessor or assessment team for the type of assessment to be conducted. [NIST 800-53 CA-2 | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must develop a control assessment plan describing the scope of the assessment, including the controls and control enhancements under assessment, assessment procedures to determine control effectiveness, and the assessment environment, team, and roles/responsibilities; the plan must be reviewed and approved by the authorizing official or designated representative prior to conducting the assessment. [NIST 800-53 CA-2 | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must assess the controls in the system and its environment of operation to determine the extent to which they are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting established security and privacy requirements. NIST and FedRAMP leave the assessment frequency organization-defined; ARC-AMPE requires assessment as specified in supplemental control requirements and guidance, including a complete independent assessment of all controls over a three (3) year period — via full reassessment at ATC expiration, annually-designated control subsets across years one through three, or per CMS guidance for significant system changes — with the final ATC package delivered no less than ninety (90) days prior to ATC expiration. [NIST 800-53 CA-2 | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must produce a control assessment report documenting the results of the assessment and provide the results to [Designated Individuals or Roles]; FedRAMP specifies this includes FedRAMP and agency customers; ARC-AMPE specifies results go to the Business Owner and personnel responsible for reviewing assessment documentation and updating security/privacy documentation, with updates made within thirty (30) days of assessment completion, and CMS notified within thirty (30) days of authorization artifact updates or significant role changes. [NIST 800-53 CA-2 | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must ensure an independent assessment of all security and privacy controls is completed before an authorizing official issues an authority to operate for any newly implemented or significantly changed system, as CMS requires. [ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must employ independent assessors or assessment teams to conduct control assessments. [NIST 800-53 CA-2(1) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE CA-2(1) AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must include specialized assessment activities (announced or unannounced) as part of control assessments annually, such as in-depth monitoring, security instrumentation, automated security test cases, vulnerability scanning, malicious user testing, insider threat assessment, performance and load testing, data leakage/loss assessment, or other [Designated Forms of Assessment]. [NIST 800-53 CA-2(2) High]
- Security Program / GRC must leverage the results of control assessments performed by [External Organization] on [Designated System] when the assessment meets [Designated Requirements]; FedRAMP specifies leveraging results from any FedRAMP Recognized independent assessment service. [NIST 800-53 CA-2(3) | FedRAMP CA-2(3)]

## 8. Plan of Action and Milestones

- Security Program / GRC must develop a plan of action and milestones (POA&M) for the system, tracked in the [Ticketing System] and reflected in the risk register, to document planned remediation actions to correct weaknesses or deficiencies noted during control assessments and to reduce or eliminate known vulnerabilities in the system. [NIST 800-53 CA-5 | ARC-AMPE CA-5 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must update the existing POA&M based on findings from control assessments, independent audits or reviews, and continuous monitoring activities, at the frequency documented in Example Org's Information Security Continuous Monitoring (ISCM) strategy, per ARC-AMPE; the POA&M must be maintained throughout the system lifecycle starting with development, including scheduled completion dates, milestones with dates, appropriate risk levels, detailed weakness descriptions, and all findings (self-discovered or via assessment); ARC-AMPE further requires delivery of a fully updated and accurate POA&M to CMS quarterly (January 31, April 30, July 31, October 31). [NIST 800-53 CA-5 | ARC-AMPE CA-5 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must ensure the accuracy, currency, and availability of the plan of action and milestones for the system using [Designated Automated Mechanisms]. [NIST 800-53 CA-5(1)]

## 9. Authorization

- Security Program / GRC must ensure a senior official is assigned as the authorizing official (AO) for the system and a senior official is assigned as the AO for common controls available for inheritance by organizational systems. [NIST 800-53 CA-6 | ARC-AMPE CA-6 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must ensure that, before commencing operations, the AO for the system accepts the use of common controls inherited by the system and authorizes the system to operate, recording the decision in the authorization decision record; the AO for common controls must authorize the use of those controls for inheritance by organizational systems. [NIST 800-53 CA-6 | ARC-AMPE CA-6 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must ensure authorizations are updated at least every three (3) years for all entities (except Direct Enrollment Technology Providers, which must update at least every one (1) year), when significant security breaches occur, when there is a significant change to the system or its operating environment, or prior to expiration of a current authorization, per ARC-AMPE; Example Org must notify CMS of significant/major changes prior to making the change. [NIST 800-53 CA-6 | ARC-AMPE CA-6 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must employ a joint authorization process for the system involving multiple authorizing officials from the same organization. [NIST 800-53 CA-6(1)]
- Security Program / GRC must employ a joint authorization process for the system involving multiple authorizing officials, including at least one from an organization external to the organization conducting the authorization. [NIST 800-53 CA-6(2)]

## 10. Continuous Monitoring

- Security Program / GRC must develop a continuous monitoring strategy (system-level, and consistent with any organization-level strategy) that establishes system-level metrics to be monitored, establishes frequencies for monitoring and for assessment of control effectiveness, and includes ongoing control assessments and ongoing monitoring of metrics in accordance with the strategy. NIST and FedRAMP leave metrics and frequencies organization-defined; ARC-AMPE requires metrics based on organizational security/privacy goals and its ISCM strategy, scans of operating systems, databases, and web applications using a [Vulnerability Scanning Tool] at least once a month, and assessment of control effectiveness no less than at least every one (1) year. [NIST 800-53 CA-7 | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must correlate and analyze information generated by control assessments and monitoring, and take response actions to address the results of that analysis. [NIST 800-53 CA-7 | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must report the security and privacy status of the system to [Designated Personnel or Roles] at least every thirty (30) days (monthly), per ARC-AMPE. [NIST 800-53 CA-7 | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must follow the FedRAMP Continuous Collaborative Monitoring, Significant Change Notification, Vulnerability Detection and Response, and Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules. [FedRAMP CA-7]
- Security Program / GRC must maintain continuous monitoring records until released by the investigating authority when a system is subject to a legal investigation (e.g., insider threat); must monitor systems, appliances, devices, and applications (including databases); and must provide oversight of information security and privacy for each system, including via a [SIEM Tool] as applicable. [ARC-AMPE CA-7 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must employ independent assessors or assessment teams to monitor the controls in the system on an ongoing basis. [NIST 800-53 CA-7(1) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE CA-7(1) AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must employ trend analyses to determine if control implementations, monitoring frequency, or monitoring activity types need modification based on empirical data. [NIST 800-53 CA-7(3)]
- Security Program / GRC must ensure risk monitoring is an integral part of the continuous monitoring strategy, including effectiveness monitoring, compliance monitoring, and change monitoring; per ARC-AMPE, the continuous monitoring strategy must document processes and guidance defining effectiveness, compliance, and change monitoring as part of a holistic risk monitoring strategy. [NIST 800-53 CA-7(4) | ARC-AMPE CA-7(4) AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must employ [Designated Actions] to validate that policies are established and implemented controls are operating in a consistent manner. [NIST 800-53 CA-7(5)]
- Security Program / GRC must ensure the accuracy, currency, and availability of monitoring results for the system using [Designated Automated Mechanisms]. [NIST 800-53 CA-7(6)]

## 11. Penetration Testing

- Security Program / GRC must conduct penetration testing at least every one (1) year on the documented system and its full boundary as agreed with testers in the Rules of Engagement, per ARC-AMPE, and must also perform testing when new risks/threats are identified or upon CMS request. [NIST 800-53 CA-8 High | FedRAMP CA-8 | ARC-AMPE CA-8 AE Mandatory]
- Penetration testing must be treated as part of vulnerability detection and is subject to the FedRAMP Vulnerability Detection and Response rules. [FedRAMP CA-8]
- The Penetration Testing Rules of Engagement must specify the scope of systems/components to be tested and any exclusions, and must be agreed upon and co-signed by both the system Authorizing Official and the penetration testing organization official; testing on production systems must minimize the risk of information corruption or service outage; scanning must include evaluation of embedded structures and interactive content; results must be searchable and provided in a CMS-compliant format; test information sources include systems, appliances, devices, services, and applications (including databases); organization-directed information collection requests must be fulfilled within the specified timeframe; and reports must be provided to CMS summarizing findings, significance, impact, risk, and remediation plans, including underlying raw security information/results in unaltered format. [ARC-AMPE CA-8 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must employ an independent penetration testing agent or team, approved by Example Org's CISO or equivalent per ARC-AMPE, to perform penetration testing on the system or system components. [NIST 800-53 CA-8(1) High | ARC-AMPE CA-8(1) AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must employ [Designated Red-Team Exercises] to simulate adversary attempts to compromise organizational systems in accordance with applicable rules of engagement. [NIST 800-53 CA-8(2)]
- Security Program / GRC must employ a penetration testing process that includes announced and/or unannounced attempts, conducted annually, to bypass or circumvent controls associated with physical access points to the facility. [NIST 800-53 CA-8(3)]

## 12. Risk Response

- Security Program / GRC must respond to findings from security and privacy assessments, monitoring, and audits in accordance with Example Org's risk tolerance, using options such as mitigating risk (implementing new or strengthened controls), accepting risk with appropriate justification/rationale, sharing or transferring risk, or avoiding risk, recording the decision in the risk register. [NIST 800-53 RA-7 | FedRAMP RA-7 | ARC-AMPE RA-7 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must follow the FedRAMP Vulnerability Detection and Response and Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules. [FedRAMP RA-7]
- Security Program / GRC must discuss risk acceptance with CMS prior to actual acceptance to ensure agreement on approach and mitigations; risk-accepted findings must be documented and tracked in the POA&M and risk register with full detail in the risk acceptance form. [ARC-AMPE RA-7 AE Mandatory]

## 13. Contingency Planning (Risk-Related)

- Security Program / GRC must establish and implement, as needed, policies and procedures for responding to an emergency or other occurrence (e.g., fire, vandalism, system failure, natural disaster) that damages systems containing electronic protected health information. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(7)(i)]
- Security Program / GRC must establish and implement procedures to create and maintain retrievable exact copies of electronic protected health information using the [Backup System]. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(A)]
- Security Program / GRC must establish and implement, as needed, procedures to restore any loss of data. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(B)]
- Security Program / GRC must establish and implement, as needed, procedures to enable continuation of critical business processes for protection of the security of electronic protected health information while operating in emergency mode. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(C)]
- Security Program / GRC must implement procedures for periodic testing and revision of contingency plans. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(D)]
- Security Program / GRC must assess the relative criticality of specific applications and data in support of other contingency plan components. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(E)]

## 14. Evidence and Recordkeeping

Security Program / GRC maintains the following artifacts as evidence that this process is operating, and is accountable for their accuracy, currency, and retention:

| Artifact                      | Content                                                                                                                                                                    | Generated/Updated By                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Risk register                 | Security categorization decisions, risk assessment results, supply chain risk assessments, POA&M items and remediation status, risk response and risk acceptance decisions | Sections 4, 5, 8, and 12 activities, performed by Security Program / GRC                                   |
| Authorization decision record | Authorizing official acceptance of common controls, system authorization to operate, and authorization update decisions                                                    | Section 9 activities, performed by Security Program / GRC in coordination with the authorizing official(s) |

Security Program / GRC must ensure both artifacts are kept current and available to support the reviews, reports, and notifications described throughout this Standard, and must review this Standard and its underlying process annually, consistent with the review requirements set out in Section 3.
